name: Feverfew
short: Trials report only mild, transient effects (mainly stomach upset and mouth ulcers). One case report linked it to bleeding. Human pregnancy safety is unstudied.
text: In a Cochrane review of six randomised trials for migraine prevention, only mild and transient adverse events were reported, most commonly gastrointestinal complaints and mouth ulcers, and no major safety concerns were identified. A single case report described vaginal bleeding and altered coagulation test results in a woman taking feverfew; its authors advised caution in people planning elective surgery, with coagulation disorders or taking antithrombotic drugs. Feverfew is traditionally avoided in pregnancy, but no human studies confirm this; a preliminary rat study found smaller fetuses with exposure and its authors called for a full reproductive study (animal data).
